entries.title: Library test: the Mudling (style key look)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ILLUSTRATION. Return exactly one image.

The attached picture is the style key. Paint one new picture in exactly its painting style: the same dense painted texture, fine brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm lamplight and crisp detail.

A MUDLING, a small friendly mud monster, knee high: a rounded lump of brown mud with a puddle base, two stubby mud arms, big round shiny eyes, a small open mouth, and a little green sprout with two leaves on top of its head. It stands on a plain flat magenta background, full body, facing the viewer, a curious friendly look. No other characters, no text.

entries.title: Grace: hero pose (cozy sweats, new style)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ILLUSTRATION. Return exactly one image, nothing else. One character, no grid, no second pose.

WHAT THIS IS
The hero pose of GRACE for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: the master reference every other picture of her will copy.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family. Match its painting style exactly: the dense jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light and crisp detail. Match how it draws a child, her head size and her body proportions, as in the key's Grace.
2. The SCHOOL YARD PAINTING. This is the texture target. Paint Grace with the same dense painted texture on skin, hair and fabric, the same fine visible brushwork and the same crisp dark-edged detail as the foliage and brick.
3. A HEIGHT CHART of grey shapes. It shows SIZE ONLY. Do not copy the grey shapes, the grid or the text. Use it to check that Grace is a 9 year old, 4 feet 2 inches tall.
4. GRACE's older reference picture. Use it for her FACE, hair and the yellow squishy keychain ONLY. Her outfit there is old, see GRACE'S OUTFIT. Do not copy how it is rendered: it is smooth and glossy, and the new picture must be painted like attachment 1. The magenta background in the attachments is not part of the picture.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Attachment 4 is for LIKENESS ONLY. Do NOT copy how it is rendered: it is smooth and glossy, and the final picture must NOT be. Repaint Grace from scratch in the painting style of attachments 1 and 2, as if the same artist painted her in the same sitting: dense painted texture on skin, hair and clothing, visible brushstrokes, crisp dark-edged detail on fabric folds, hair strands and shoe edges, deep saturated colors and rich contrast. No airbrushed skin, no smooth gradients, no glossy plastic look, no soft-focus photo look, no 3D render look. The sweatshirt and sweatpants show a knitted, fuzzy fabric texture.

THE POSE
Full body, head to feet fully in frame, standing neutral and relaxed, body turned a little (three quarter) toward the viewer, a warm natural smile, face clear and readable, hands empty and relaxed at her sides, both feet flat on the ground and fully visible. Large and centered, filling most of the height of the image, with a little space above her head and below her feet. This is the most detailed picture of the set: individual hair strands, skin, fabric weave, glitter on the shoes.

GRACE
A 9 year old girl, real height 4 feet 2 inches. Bright, confident and a little bossy: a playful, self-assured smile.

GRACE'S OUTFIT
Loose, comfy, cozy sweats: an oversized soft lavender sweatshirt with sleeves a little too long and a relaxed fit, and baggy heather-gray sweatpants, slightly bunched at the ankles. Cute glittery sneakers in pink and silver glitter with white soles and bright laces. Her yellow squishy keychain clipped at her hip on the sweatpants waistband, exactly as in attachment 4. No leotard, no gym outfit.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a real person, shown full body, painted by hand in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style with visible painted texture and fine, detailed brushwork, like the style key. Gently simplified shapes. Slightly stylized features that keep a clear likeness. Clothing details are drawn clearly.
- Caricature proportions for a child: a clearly oversized head, one quarter of her full height from the top of her hair to her chin, noticeably bigger than a real child's, a small slim body, small hands and small feet, large expressive eyes and a warm, slightly exaggerated expression. The head is as large relative to her body as the style key's Grace, a caricature, not a realistic child. The face keeps a clear likeness of the real child in attachment 4.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp edges with fine detail. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

LIKENESS
Keep the face of attachment 4: the exact face shape, cheeks, nose, lips, smile, eyebrows, eye shape and color, skin tone and the hair color, length, parting, volume and texture. Exaggerate only the head size and the expression, never the individual features. Do not beautify, age up or age down her, and do not turn her into a generic child.

BACKGROUND
One flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on the character. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on her edges or hair strands. No ground, no shadow, no gradient, no border, no text, no labels.

NEVER substitute. Draw only Grace. Family friendly for ages 6 and up. If anything is unclear, draw her standing relaxed and smiling as described.

entries.title: Grace: hero pose step 1, painted in the school yard

IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ILLUSTRATION. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
A painting of GRACE standing alone in the school yard, for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game. She is painted INSIDE the school yard scene, in the same sitting by the same artist, so that she has exactly the same painted texture as the scene around her.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The school yard painting. This is the BACKGROUND and the STYLE TO MATCH. Keep the school building, paths, signs, lamps, parking area and playground exactly as painted, same framing, nothing removed. Match its dense, jewel-toned painted texture, its fine visible brushwork, its deep saturated colors, its warm lamplight and its level of detail in the character.
2. GRACE's older reference picture. Use it for her FACE, hair and the yellow squishy keychain ONLY. Her outfit there is old, see GRACE'S OUTFIT. Do not copy how it is rendered: it is smooth and glossy, and the new picture must not be.
3. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in this same school yard. Match how it paints people and how it draws a child, including Grace's head size and body proportions.
4. A HEIGHT CHART of grey shapes. It shows SIZE ONLY. Do not copy the grey shapes, the grid or the text. Use it to check that Grace is a 9 year old, 4 feet 2 inches tall.
The magenta background in attachment 2 is not part of the picture. Ignore it.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Attachment 2 is for LIKENESS ONLY. Repaint Grace from scratch in the exact painting style of attachment 1, as if the same artist painted the whole canvas in one sitting: the same dense painted texture on skin, hair and fabric, the same fine visible brushwork, the same crisp dark-edged detail on fabric folds, hair strands and shoe edges, the same deep saturated colors and rich contrast, the same fine detail as the foliage and brick. No airbrushed skin, no smooth gradients, no glossy plastic look, no soft-focus photo look, no 3D render look. Her face keeps the likeness but is painted with the same brushwork as the rest of the picture. The sweatshirt and sweatpants show a knitted, fuzzy fabric texture.

THE SCENE
Use the school yard painting as the whole background. Grace is the only person in the picture. She stands large and centered on the wide paved walkway in the middle of the picture, full body from the top of her hair to the soles of her sneakers, her feet on the paving. She stands neutral and relaxed, body turned a little (three quarter) toward the viewer, a warm natural smile, face clear and readable, hands empty and relaxed at her sides, both feet flat and fully visible. She casts a soft shadow on the paving.

GRACE'S OUTFIT (overrides her reference picture's clothes)

- She is lit by the SAME light as the background: warm orange lamplight from the nearby lamp posts and the school windows, cool blue-violet dusk sky light as fill, with warm rim light on hair and shoulders.
- Clean, crisp edges with fine detail. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

LIKENESS
Keep the face of attachment 2: the exact face shape, cheeks, nose, lips, smile, eyebrows, eye shape and color, skin tone and the hair color, length, parting, volume and texture. Exaggerate only the head size and the expression, never the individual features. Do not beautify, age up or age down her.

NEVER substitute. Draw only Grace. No other people, no text, no labels, no captions, no speech balloons. Family friendly for ages 6 and up. If anything is unclear, draw her standing relaxed and smiling in the school yard as described.

entries.title: Grace: walking sheet 3 x 3 (painted, on magenta)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE CHARACTER WALKING SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
The walking sheet of GRACE for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: nine walking frames, a 3 by 3 grid, used to walk her around a town.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. GRACE's master picture: a finished painting of her on a flat magenta background. This is the ONLY source for her face, hair, outfit, colors, painted texture and brushwork. Draw her EXACTLY like this in every frame: same face, same hair, same clothes, same prints and fabric texture, same colors, same painted look and level of detail. The magenta in this picture is the background to use here too.
2. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. It shows how this game paints people and how it draws a child. Match its dense, jewel-toned painted texture and fine visible brushwork on every part of Grace: skin, hair, fabric and shoes.
3. A HEIGHT CHART of grey shapes. It shows SIZE ONLY. Do not copy the grey shapes, the grid or the text. Use it to keep Grace a 9 year old, 4 feet 2 inches tall.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look painted by the same hand as attachments 1 and 2: dense painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, crisp detail on hair strands, fabric folds and shoe edges. No airbrushed skin, no smooth gradients, no glossy plastic look, no soft-focus look, no 3D render look. The sweatshirt and sweatpants keep the knitted, fuzzy fabric texture of attachment 1.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a real person, shown full body, painted by hand in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style with visible painted texture and fine, detailed brushwork, like the illustrated school-yard painting the style key lives in. Gently simplified shapes. Slightly stylized features that keep a clear likeness. Clothing prints and patterns are drawn in clear detail so every motif is readable.
- Caricature proportions for a child: an oversized head a little under half of the full body height, a small body, small hands and small feet, large expressive eyes and a warm, slightly exaggerated expression. The head size in attachment 1 wins over any number in this paragraph: in every frame the head is exactly as large, compared with the body, as it is in attachment 1.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp edges with fine detail. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

GRACE
A 9 year old girl. Long, wavy, golden-blond hair past her shoulders. Oversized soft lavender sweatshirt with sleeves a little too long, baggy heather-gray sweatpants bunched at the ankles, pink and silver glitter sneakers with white soles and bright laces, a yellow squishy keychain clipped at her hip on the sweatpants waistband, visible whenever that hip is visible. Keep every detail of attachment 1. For the back view, extend the outfit plainly and consistently: the back of the sweatshirt has the same knitted texture, her long hair falls down her back. Never invent a new accessory, hairstyle or color.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A grid of 3 columns by 3 rows of equal square cells, 256 x 256 pixels each, so the full image is 768 x 768. If your tool offers a larger square size, keep exactly 3 columns and 3 rows.
- Exactly 9 frames, one per cell, filled left to right, top to bottom, in the numbered order below.
- Camera: a character turnaround at about chest height, full body, straight on for the front and back rows and a true side profile for the third row. No top-down angle.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on Grace. Her pink sneakers must stay clearly pink, never magenta. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on her edges or hair strands. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.
- Each frame sits fully inside its cell with at least 10 percent margin. Nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.
- Same scale in every cell. The standing figure is about 150 pixels tall in its cell, from the top of the hair to the soles of the shoes. Feet on the ground rest on one horizontal line about 24 pixels above the cell bottom.
- Draw ONLY Grace. Hands empty. No effects, shadows, dust, motion lines, sparkles, props, other people, text or word balloons.
- The same head size, the same hair volume and the same outfit in every frame. The head is never redrawn smaller or larger from frame to frame.

THE 9 FRAMES
Row 1, facing the viewer:
1. DOWN STAND: facing the viewer, feet together, arms relaxed at her sides, a warm natural smile.
2. DOWN STEP A: facing the viewer, the foot on the viewer's right steps forward, the arm on the viewer's left swings forward.
3. DOWN STEP B: the mirror of frame 2.
Row 2, seen from behind:
4. UP STAND: seen from behind, feet together, arms at her sides, her long hair and the back of the sweatshirt fully visible.
5. UP STEP A: seen from behind, the foot on the viewer's left steps away from us, the arm on the viewer's right swings forward.
6. UP STEP B: the mirror of frame 5.
Row 3, a true side profile facing LEFT:
7. SIDE STAND: profile facing left, feet together, arms relaxed.
8. SIDE STEP A: profile facing left, the front leg forward with the heel down, the back leg trailing with the heel lifted, the near arm back and the far arm forward.
9. SIDE STEP B: profile facing left, the passing moment of the stride, the back foot lifted with a bent knee, the body slightly higher.

The two STEP frames of a row mirror each other. Arms always swing opposite to the legs. STAND frames are neutral.

Family friendly for ages 6 and up.

NEVER substitute. Do not add extra frames, merge two frames, repeat a pose, or invent props. If anything is unclear, draw Grace in the pose described, with the face, hair and outfit exactly as in attachment 1.

entries.title: Grace: battle sheet 4 x 4 (painted, on magenta)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE CHARACTER BATTLE SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
The standard battle pose sheet of GRACE for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: sixteen poses, a 4 by 4 grid. Grace is a bright, bossy, confident 9 year old, and the poses show it.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. GRACE's master picture: a finished painting of her on a flat magenta background. This is the ONLY source for her face, hair, outfit, colors, painted texture and brushwork. Draw her EXACTLY like this in every frame: same face, same hair, same clothes, same prints and fabric texture, same colors, same painted look and level of detail. The magenta in this picture is the background to use here too.

3. A HEIGHT CHART of grey shapes. It shows SIZE ONLY. Do not copy the grey shapes, the grid or the text. Use it to keep Grace a 9 year old, 4 feet 2 inches tall.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look painted by the same hand as attachments 1 and 2: dense painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, crisp detail on hair strands, fabric folds and shoe edges. No airbrushed skin, no smooth gradients, no glossy plastic look, no soft-focus look, no 3D render look. The sweatshirt and sweatpants keep the knitted, fuzzy fabric texture of attachment 1.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a real person, shown full body, painted by hand in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style with visible painted texture and fine, detailed brushwork, like the illustrated school-yard painting the style key lives in. Gently simplified shapes. Slightly stylized features that keep a clear likeness. Clothing prints and patterns are drawn in clear detail so every motif is readable.
- Caricature proportions for a child: an oversized head a little under half of the full body height, a small body, small hands and small feet, large expressive eyes and a warm, slightly exaggerated expression. The head size in attachment 1 wins over any number in this paragraph: in every frame the head is exactly as large, compared with the body, as it is in attachment 1.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp edges with fine detail. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

GRACE
A 9 year old girl. Long, wavy, golden-blond hair past her shoulders. Oversized soft lavender sweatshirt with sleeves a little too long, baggy heather-gray sweatpants bunched at the ankles, pink and silver glitter sneakers with white soles and bright laces, a yellow squishy keychain clipped at her hip on the sweatpants waistband, visible whenever that hip is visible. Keep every detail of attachment 1 in every frame, including crouched, leaning and sitting poses. Never invent a new accessory, hairstyle or color. No leotard, no gym outfit.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A grid of 4 columns by 4 rows of equal square cells, 256 x 256 pixels each, so the full image is 1024 x 1024. If your tool offers a larger square size, keep exactly 4 columns and 4 rows.
- Exactly 16 frames, one per cell, filled left to right, top to bottom, in the numbered order below.
- Grace FACES LEFT in every frame: a side or three-quarter view from slightly above, a hero facing an off-screen opponent on the left in a family-friendly fantasy game. Her face stays visible and turned toward the left, except where a frame says her head is bowed or tilted back.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on Grace. Her pink sneakers must stay clearly pink, never magenta. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on her edges or hair strands. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.
- Each frame sits fully inside its cell with at least 10 percent margin. Nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.
- Same scale in every cell. Never rescale a frame to fit a pose: crouched poses get shorter and lunges get wider. Feet on the ground rest on one horizontal line about 24 pixels above the cell bottom.
- Draw ONLY Grace. Hands empty. No effects, shadows, dust, motion lines, sparkles, props, other people, text or word balloons.
- The same head size, the same hair volume and the same outfit in every frame. The head is never redrawn smaller or larger from frame to frame, whatever the pose.

THE 16 FRAMES (each clearly different from the others)
1. IDLE A: battle stance, feet shoulder width apart, knees slightly bent, hands loose, a bright, confident expression aimed at the off-screen opponent.
2. IDLE B: the same stance a moment later, chest risen with a breath, one hand flicking her hair back over her shoulder.
3. WALK A: striding left, the near foot forward, the opposite arm swinging.
4. WALK B: the opposite step.
5. HIP: standing, both hands on her hips, chin lifted, a bossy, impatient look.
6. ACT: right arm extended to the left, palm up, presenting something, a small proud smile.
7. WIND-UP: body twisted away from the opponent, arm cocked back, weight on the back leg, eyes narrowed.
8. SWING: follow-through, lunging far forward to the left, arm at full extension, front knee bent, mouth open in a shout.
9. SPREAD: feet planted, both arms flung wide, chest out, chin up, announcing something with a big grin.
10. GUARD: crouched low, forearms crossed in front of her chest and face, chin tucked, one eye peeking over her arms.
11. FLINCH: startled, recoiling, leaning back and to the right, head tilted back, eyes squeezed shut, one foot lifted.
12. TIRED: kneeling on one knee, one hand resting on that knee, head hanging, a tired little pout.
13. NAP: sitting on the ground facing left, legs out in front, head drooping and eyes closed as if taking a nap, arms relaxed in her lap.
14. CHEER A: victory, one fist pumped high, the other hand on her hip, a big grin.
15. CHEER B: both fists overhead, laughing, heels lifted.
16. SIGNATURE (BOSSY POINT): one hand on her hip, the other arm stretched straight out to the left with her index finger pointing at the off-screen opponent, chin up, one eyebrow raised, a confident, commanding smile.

Family friendly for ages 6 and up.

NEVER substitute. Do not add extra frames, merge two frames, repeat a pose, or invent props. If anything is unclear, draw Grace in the pose described, with the face, hair and outfit exactly as in attachment 1 and the head size exactly as in attachment 1.
